To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have proposed a distributed training algorithm for echo state networks, and we have shown that the algorithm can achieve good prediction accuracy in a decentralized setting.

we have developed a novel, distributed algorithm to train a particular class of neural networks, the ESNs, and that this algorithm is able to exploit an additional property of the output layers of ESNs to achieve a very compact, efficient implementation of the resulting networks.
we have developed a distributed algorithm to train an ECN with sparse readouts.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a new distributed implementation of a particular class neural networks, namely ESNs, that is able to exploit a particular property of the network architecture, namely the sparsity of the readout layer.
the development of a novel distributed algorithm for training ESNs with sparse output weights, and with the evaluation of its performances in two benchmark prediction scenarios.
the distributed implementation of ESNs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for the two benchmarks considered in this work, the performance of the proposed distributed algorithm, in terms of both accuracy and computational complexity, is comparable with those of the centralized counterpart.
the proposed algorithm is very promising, as it can be used to train ESNs with very low communication overhead, and it is also able to achieve good prediction performance.
the proposed algorithm, in the case of sparse ESNs, is a viable alternative to the state-of-the-art distributed algorithms for the training of recurrent neural networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed distributed training scheme, when combined with sparse output layers, can provide a viable and scalable alternative to centralized ESN training.
the proposed approach allows to achieve good performance in terms of accuracy, and to reduce the computational complexity, while preserving the distributed nature of the training algorithm.
the proposed algorithm can efficiently train a distributed reservoir computing system with sparse readouts, which is a very interesting feature from a hardware implementation point of view.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed distributed training scheme, based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm, allows for the development of sparse ESNs with very efficient implementations.
, even in the case of sparse ESNs, the proposed distributed algorithm is able to achieve the performance of the centralized counterpart.

the proposed distributed algorithm, when combined with the sparsity constraint of the output weights, can achieve a performance close to that obtained with a centralized implementation of the ESN, but with much lower computational complexity.
